title: Derived duality for perfect complexes
statement: Let $B$ be a commutative ring and let $C\in D(B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], formed with localization universe equal to the coefficient universe and equipped with a braided monoidal structure. Assume that $C$ is perfect [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], meaning represented by a bounded complex of finitely generated projective $B$-modules [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Then $R\operatorname{Hom}_B(C,B)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] is perfect, and the canonical evaluation map $C\to R\operatorname{Hom}_B(R\operatorname{Hom}_B(C,B),B)$ is an isomorphism in $D(B)$.

source.place: Tag 07VI, lemma-dual-perfect-complex (the bounded finite-projective Hom model and signed double-dual evaluation).

proof.text: By [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], choose a bounded finite-projective complex $P$, supported in $[a,b]$, and an isomorphism $e:QP\xrightarrow{\sim}C$. Put $O=B[0]$, $E=H(P,O)$ and $F=H(E,O)$. By [lem-trf-finite-projective-hom-dual-involution], $E$ is bounded finite-projective, supported in $[-b,-a]$, and the signed evaluation $\delta_P:P\xrightarrow{\sim}F$ is a chain isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 07VI, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, bounded finite-projective Hom dual and signed double evaluation; Tag 0FNG, section-sign-rules; actual Hom coordinates and differential in section-hom-complexes (Tag 0A8H).

proof.text: Both $P$ and $E$ are bounded above with projective terms. Apply [lem-trf-projective-bidual-representative-comparison] with $T=P$, $D=E$: it identifies the ordinary-module and one-object ringed-site Hom models, supplies the two K-injective-augmentation quasi-isomorphisms, and gives $\gamma_P:QE\cong(QP)^\vee$, $\gamma_E:QF\cong(QE)^\vee$. Thus $(QP)^\vee$ is represented by the bounded finite-projective complex $E$. Since $e^\vee:C^\vee\cong(QP)^\vee$, [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex] proves that $C^\vee$ is perfect.

proof.text: The same representative comparison gives $(\gamma_P)^\vee b_{QP}=\gamma_E Q(\delta_P)$. The right side is invertible, since localization takes the chain isomorphism $\delta_P$ to an isomorphism. Since $(\gamma_P)^\vee$ is also invertible, $b_{QP}$ is invertible.

source.place: Tag 0A66, lemma-RHom-out-of-projective, including the map to the K-injective Hom model; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0A97, lemma-internal-hom-evaluate, coefficient-unit transpose and naturality; sites.tex Tag 00X9, section-topoi, punctual topos. proof.text: Naturality from [lem-trf-projective-bidual-representative-comparison] gives $b_C e=e^{\vee\vee}b_{QP}$, hence $b_C=e^{\vee\vee}b_{QP}e^{-1}$. Each factor is invertible, proving that the Koszul transpose $b_C$ is invertible. This uses the actual canonical map, rather than merely an unspecified isomorphism of its source and target.

proof.text: The statement fixes the derived tensor $\otimes^{\mathbf L}_B$ with unit $O=B[0]$ and lets the braiding $\sigma$ be arbitrary; its canonical evaluation is formed with $\sigma$. Through the one-object identification of [lem-trf-projective-bidual-representative-comparison], [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] makes $D(B)$ closed: $-\otimes^{\mathbf L}_BL$ is left adjoint to $R\operatorname{Hom}_B(L,-)$, with coefficient evaluation as counit. So the canonical evaluation is $b^\sigma_C$, the transpose of $\mathrm{ev}_{C,O}\circ\sigma_{C,C^\vee}$; for the Koszul symmetry it is the map $b_C$ of Steps 3--4. Since $C$ is perfect, [lem-zl-ring-derived-dualizable-perfect] makes it dualizable for $\otimes^{\mathbf L}_B$. Then [lem-trf-dualizable-braided-canonical-bidual] shows that $b^\sigma_C$ is an isomorphism for every braiding $\sigma$. This proves the second conclusion as stated, and Steps 3--4 are its explicit Koszul case.
